stem: Acyclovir is used to treat viral infections such as which of the following sets?

options.label: A
options.text: Influenza, respiratory syncytial virus and COVID-19
options.misconception: Assumes acyclovir is a broad-spectrum antiviral for respiratory viruses.
options.explanation: Influenza, RSV and SARS-CoV-2 are RNA respiratory viruses; acyclovir needs activation by herpesvirus thymidine kinase and does not treat them.

options.label: B
options.misconception: None — acyclovir treats chickenpox, shingles and genital herpes.
options.explanation: MedlinePlus lists chickenpox, herpes zoster (shingles) and genital herpes as infections acyclovir treats; it is an antiviral that stops viral spread.

options.label: C
options.text: Hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV infection
options.misconception: Assumes any nucleoside-analog antiviral also treats chronic hepatitis or HIV.
options.explanation: Hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV need their own antiviral classes, such as nucleos(t)ide analogs, direct-acting antivirals and antiretrovirals.

options.label: D
options.text: Genital warts, common warts and molluscum contagiosum
options.misconception: Links acyclovir to all genital and skin viral lesions, not just herpesvirus infections.
options.explanation: Warts are caused by HPV and molluscum contagiosum by a poxvirus; neither is treated with acyclovir, which targets herpesviruses.

options.label: E
options.misconception: Assumes acyclovir treats every childhood viral rash illness, not just varicella.
options.explanation: Measles, mumps and rubella are prevented with MMR vaccine and managed supportively; acyclovir has no role against them.

context: Learning objective: Acyclovir is an antiviral used to treat chickenpox, herpes zoster (shingles) and genital herpes.
